verses.text: At that time Judah left his brothers and went down to stay with a man from Adullam named Hirah.
There Judah met the daughter of a Canaanite man named Shua. He married her and slept with her.
She became pregnant and gave birth to a son, who was named Er.
She became pregnant again and gave birth to a son, and she named him Onan.
She gave birth to yet another son and named him Shelah. He was born at Kezib.
Judah chose a wife for Er, his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.
But Judah's firstborn, Er, was wicked in the LORD's eyes, so the LORD put him to death.
Then Judah said to Onan, "Sleep with your brother's wife and do your duty as her brother-in-law. Give your brother children who will carry on his name."

But Onan knew that the children would not be counted as his. So whenever he slept with his brother's wife, he made sure she could not become pregnant, so that he would not give children to his brother.
What he did was wicked in the LORD's eyes, so the LORD put him to death too.

Then Judah said to his daughter-in-law Tamar, "Live as a widow in your father's house until my son Shelah grows up." He thought, "He might die too, just like his brothers." So Tamar went to live in her father's house.

After a long time Judah's wife, the daughter of Shua, died. When Judah had finished mourning, he went up to Timnah, to the men who were cutting the wool from his sheep. His friend Hirah the Adullamite went with him.
Tamar was told, "Your father-in-law is on his way to Timnah to cut the wool from his sheep."

So she took off her widow's clothes and covered herself with a veil to hide who she was. Then she sat down at the entrance to Enaim, which is on the road to Timnah. She did this because she saw that Shelah had grown up, but she had not been given to him as his wife.
When Judah saw her, he thought she was a prostitute, because she had covered her face.
Not realising that she was his daughter-in-law, he went over to her by the roadside and said, "Come, let me sleep with you." "What will you give me to sleep with you?" she asked.
"I will send you a young goat from my flock," he said. "Will you give me something as a pledge until you send it?" she asked.
He said, "What pledge should I give you?" "Your seal and its cord, and the walking stick in your hand," she answered. So he gave them to her and slept with her, and she became pregnant by him.
After she left, she took off her veil and put on her widow's clothes again.
Meanwhile, Judah sent the young goat by his friend the Adullamite to get back his pledge from the woman, but he could not find her.
He asked the men who lived there, "Where is the shrine prostitute who was beside the road at Enaim?" "There has never been any shrine prostitute here," they said.
So he went back to Judah and said, "I did not find her. Besides, the men who live there said, 'There has never been any shrine prostitute here.'"
Then Judah said, "Let her keep what she has, or we will become a laughing stock. After all, I did send her this young goat, but you could not find her."
About three months later Judah was told, "Your daughter-in-law Tamar has acted like a prostitute, and as a result she is now pregnant." Judah said, "Bring her out and have her burned to death!"

As she was being brought out, she sent a message to her father-in-law. "I am pregnant by the man who owns these," she said. And she added, "See if you recognise whose seal and cord and walking stick these are."
Judah recognised them and said, "She is more in the right than I am, because I would not give her to my son Shelah." And he did not sleep with her again.
When the time came for her to give birth, there were twin boys in her womb.
As she was giving birth, one of them put out his hand. So the woman helping her took a red thread and tied it on his wrist and said, "This one came out first."
But when he pulled his hand back, his brother came out. She said, "So this is how you have broken out!" And he was named Perez, which means "breaking out".
Then his brother, who had the red thread on his wrist, came out. And he was named Zerah, which means "bright red".
